- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 3–7 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% per day.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model fails to adjust quickly; delay peak forecast by 1–3 days and smooth transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), model often overfits recent noise; use 18-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply bias correction by adding 1–3% to early days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
